title: `notifications/resources/updated`
description: Per-resource change notifications, opted into by listing URIs in a `subscriptions/listen` request and delivered as `notifications/resources/updated`.
question: Can the agent watch a single resource for changes?
why: This is the difference between an agent that re-reads everything on a timer and one that reacts when a specific thing changes. In 2026-07-28 it also requires the new subscription stream, so a framework still written against `resources/subscribe` cannot do it at all.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers publishing this. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1 has no subscribe API. Opening `mcp.client.subscriptions.listen(MCPServerStdio.session, resource_subscriptions=[uri])` on the raw SDK session delivered the update, and closing it stopped updates. That route belongs to the SDK, not the adapter.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: `MCPToolset` has no subscribe API. Opening `mcp.client.subscriptions.listen` with `resource_subscriptions=[uri]` on `MCPToolset.client.session` delivered the update, and closing it stopped updates. That route belongs to the SDK, not the adapter.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` has no subscribe method, and the `subscriptions/listen` stream it opens names tools list changes only, so a caller cannot subscribe to a resource.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient has no subscribe or unsubscribe method and no handler for resource updates. 2.0.73 adds `experimental_events`, a webhook API for `events/subscribe` and `events/unsubscribe`, which is a separate surface and does not cover resource updates.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServer` interface has `listResources`, `listResourceTemplates` and `readResource`, but no `resources/subscribe` method and no hook for `notifications/resources/updated`.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` has no subscribe method; a resource update arrives only through the raw `ClientSession` at `MCPTools.session.session`, with `mcp.client.subscriptions.listen(session, resource_subscriptions=[uri])`.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no subscribe API. The update arrives only through `mcp.client.subscriptions.listen(session, resource_subscriptions=[uri])` on the caller's `mcp.Client.session`.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): the `resourceSubscriptions` server option subscribes at connect and `onResourcesUpdated` receives the update, but the adapter has no unsubscribe method and the list is fixed for the connection.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): there is no API that sends `resources/subscribe` or `resources/unsubscribe`.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `Subscribe` on.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `McpClient.SubscribeToResourceAsync` sends `resources/subscribe`, which 2026-07-28 removed; the server answered "Method not found", and the client offers no `subscriptions/listen` route instead.
